clue.text: Divine Satie composed in a small room

indicators.note: in places the rearranged composer inside the room

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters of the name are arranged afresh, like a piece of music

explanation.surface: The French composer Erik Satie writing heavenly music in a cramped little room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like the composer at work, but it is the anagram signal; 'a small room' is a monk's or prisoner's cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine and celestial are synonyms, both meaning heavenly or godlike.

clue.text: Follow trial about husband

indicators.note: about means the trial goes round the next piece

parts.note: a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: Someone keeps track of a court case involving a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone in pursuit is to run after them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Philanderer ends in buffet with a woman, finally

indicators.note: in places the ending word inside the word for a blow

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or buffet
dies means ends, as a sound dies away

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of woman

explanation.surface: A womaniser meets his end at a buffet alongside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' reads as a meal but is a verb meaning to strike, and 'ends' is a verb meaning expires.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanderer chases women casually, which is the idiom for a womaniser.

clue.text: Work of fiction in which politician keeps trousers on

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the trousers above the politician

parts.note: shorts are short trousers
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A novel in which a politician never removes his trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief piece of prose fiction is a genre name for a tale shorter than a novel.

clue.text: Bill, affectedly embarrassed, is discourteous

indicators.note: affectedly suggests the name is put on in an altered, artificial form

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: Bill, blushing in a put-on way, is being rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly brought up is rude, so the compound adjective means impolite.

clue.text: Ambassadors for the French tycoon

parts.note: le is French for the
Bill Gates is the Microsoft tycoon

explanation.surface: Envoys working for a French business magnate.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal legates are envoys, so ambassadors is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Tie leaves back

indicators.note: back means the verb for leaves is read from its end

parts.note: parts means leaves, departs

explanation.surface: A necktie is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a verb, PARTS, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie something with a band is to fasten it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Location of stated exhibition

indicators.note: stated means the word for exhibition is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sight is something exhibited, a spectacle

explanation.surface: Where the announced exhibition will take place.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position, a straightforward synonym of location.

clue.text: Always got up to capture English bird

indicators.note: to capture means the turned word takes in the next letter
in a down clue, got up means the word for always is read upwards

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always rose early to catch an English bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: Open lurid assortment that's stolen

indicators.note: an assortment mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unwrap a garish selection of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To purloin is to steal, so the past participle means taken illicitly.

clue.text: Increase one form of insecticide with oxygen

parts.note: a means one
DDT is a well-known insecticide
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Boost an insecticide by adding oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: To add to something is to augment it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: A long way in a short time?

definitions.text: A long way in a short time?

parts.words: A long way in a short time?
parts.note: a unit of astronomical distance whose name sounds like a measure of time, and light covers it in what is cosmically a short while

explanation.walkthrough: The unit sounds like time but measures distance, the distance light travels in twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use this unit for huge distances, so it is literally a long way.

clue.text: The people prefer no local tax

parts.note: to elect is to choose or prefer
O is zero, nothing
rates were the British local property tax

explanation.surface: The public would rather not pay council tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the property tax British councils levied before council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters as a body are the people who choose a government.

clue.text: Ruler found in throne room

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A monarch discovered in the throne room.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor, an example of a ruler.

clue.text: One has faith in investments

parts.note: a unit is one
trusts means has faith in

explanation.surface: A believer who puts faith in investing.
explanation.walkthrough: A unit trust is a British pooled investment fund, like an American mutual fund.
explanation.definitionFit: These pooled funds are financial products, examples of investments.

clue.text: Stand-in has lad with his mouth watering

parts.note: a temp stands in for another worker
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A temporary worker has a boy drooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose mouth waters is enticed, drawn in by temptation.

clue.text: Bloated stomach egghead's to detect

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
the head of egg is its first letter E
to scent is to detect by smell

explanation.surface: A tummy that an intellectual has to examine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumescent means swollen, so bloated is a close synonym.

clue.text: He induces sleep with morphine, initially in the sanatorium

indicators.note: in places the conjunction and the drug's opening letter inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
and means with

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of morphine

explanation.surface: A sanatorium patient sent to sleep with morphine.
explanation.definitionFit: The folklore figure sprinkles sand to make children drowsy.

clue.text: Prelate finds new character in Othello

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and symbol inside Othello

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice
a sign is a written character or symbol

explanation.surface: A churchman discovers a fresh personality in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Catholic cleric bears this honorific title, a churchman of rank.

clue.text: Poacher's concern requires words of comfort repeated quietly

parts.note: a mantra is a soothing phrase said over and over
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A poacher needs reassuring phrases murmured softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A poacher must beware the device set to catch trespassers on an estate.

clue.text: Plain tart takes in Romeo's look

indicators.note: takes in means the pastry holds the next pieces

parts.note: a tart is a pie
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A simple pastry adopts Romeo's appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the tart but is a noun, a grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide treeless grassland in North America is a type of plain.

clue.text: A Parisian has day with boy not properly adjusted

parts.note: un is French for a
Tu is an abbreviation for Tuesday
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman spends a day with a lad who is a bit unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument out of tune has not been set right, so it is badly adjusted.

clue.text: Actor sees drunken viscount caught out

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order
out means the letter for caught is removed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An actor watches a tipsy nobleman being dismissed in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from VISCOUNT, and 'drunken' rearranges the remaining VISOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ustinov was a celebrated British actor and writer.

clue.text: Faction agreed to accommodate Charlie

indicators.note: to accommodate means the word for agreed makes room for the letter

parts.note: set means agreed or fixed, as in a set price
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A splinter group consents to take Charlie in.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway religious or political group is a faction.

clue.text: Load vehicle with spirit

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
go means spirit or energy

explanation.surface: Fill a car with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests drink, but it is GO, meaning vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship or plane are its freight, a noun synonym of load.

clue.text: See it rated badly in the festive season

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Look how poorly it was reviewed over the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The weeks after Easter Sunday form a Christian festival season.

clue.text: Turn out dying to get mounted

parts.note: end means dying, as in one's end
up means mounted, on horseback

explanation.surface: Finish up dying in order to ride a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out a certain way is to finish that way, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Leather cloak

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin used as leather
to cloak is to conceal from view

explanation.surface: A leather cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal skin is leather, and to conceal is to cloak.

clue.text: Hearing tall story by boy previously

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a lie is a tall story
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone heard a boy's fib at an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done before now happened at a prior point, so the phrase means beforehand.

clue.text: Fellows hold Yankee back in council

indicators.note: back means the fellows holding the letter are then read from the end
hold means the turned word keeps the letter inside

parts.note: dons are university fellows
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: College fellows keep an American back in a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church assembly, a kind of council.

clue.text: Valuable collection lets Tory leader gallivant

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of Tory

parts.note: to rove is to wander about, to gallivant

explanation.surface: A treasure lets the Conservative party leader wander about.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a stash of treasure found or kept.

clue.text: Dope raves about spy

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An idiot ranting about an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen in secretly is to spy on a conversation.
